concerns.advisory: Parallelism is only settable at process start via a CLI flag, with no runtime option (unlike `spans.buffer.flusher.max-unhealthy-seconds` etc.), so rolling back or tuning fan-out requires a deploy/restart of the consumer.
concerns.why: `flusher_processes` is threaded from click → factory → SpanFlusher constructor; no `options.get(...)` gate was added alongside the existing flusher options.

concerns.advisory: Each flusher process constructs its own `SpansBuffer(shards)`, multiplying Redis connections, per-process Sentry app initialization, and resident memory by the number of processes on every consumer pod.
concerns.why: `_create_process_for_shards` calls `shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)` per process index, and spawn context re-initializes the app via `run_with_initialized_sentry`.

concerns.advisory: `spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy` is now emitted once per shard with a new `shard` tag instead of once per unhealthy flusher, so existing dashboards/alerts on that counter will see counts inflated by the shard fan-out and lose comparability across the deploy.
concerns.why: the `for shard in shards: metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy", tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard})` loop replaces a single `metrics.incr`.

concerns.advisory: The new metric tags use inconsistent keys — `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` on `flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` but `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` on `flusher.wait_produce` — which will split queries/dashboards that expect one tag name.

The shard tag value is a comma-joined list of shard ids whose composition depends on partition assignment and `flusher_processes`, so tag cardinality is unbounded across rebalances/config changes and previously-untagged timers/timings now carry it.

`MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` is now enforced per process index rather than globally, so a consumer with N flusher processes tolerates up to N× as many flusher restarts before raising and restarting the consumer.
concerns.why: `self.process_restarts` became a per-index dict and the threshold check is inside the per-process loop in `_ensure_processes_alive`.

concerns.why: `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())` followed by unchanged `sum(x.used ...) / sum(x.available ...)`.
